title: An analytical formulation with iterative solution for the structure-aerodynamic interaction of a variable-camber airfoil.
author: Camilo Jacob Tenório de Mello Contreras
abstract: Based on the idea of exploiting distributed structural flexibility to enhance the aerodynamics of an airfoil, the belt-rib concept was born in the framework of the Adaptive Wing Project (ADIF) at the DLR (German Aerospace Centre). The belt-rib airfoil has built-in spokes, whose primary function is to reduce the degree of freedom of the displacements and hence, to afford controllability through actuators over the surface deformation. In the present work, a mathematical model and a computer program were developed to describe the characteristics of static equilibrium of airfoils of the belt-rib type, when it is subjected to aerodynamic load and actuator activity. The aerodynamics is modelled through Theodorsen's potential flow theory for airfoils with Prandtl-Glauert compressibility correction. The structure part uses a modified Castigliano's theorem to calculate linear elastic deformations. Both parts are coupled through an iterative method. A Mathematica-based program was developed with this theory and simulations for the belt-rib are realised and analysed.
